```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Tests\Generated;

use Money\Currencies;
use Money\Currency;
use Money\Exception\ParserException;
use Money\Money;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Test;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

/**
 * @covers \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser
 */
final class DecimalMoneyParserGeneratedTest extends TestCase
{
    private Currencies $currencies;
    private Currency $currency;

    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        // Create a mock-like stub for Currencies since we can't easily instantiate the real interface without dependencies.
        // We need to satisfy the constructor requirement.
        $this->currencies = new class implements Currencies {
            public function contains(Currency $currency): bool
            {
                return true;
            }

            public function subunitFor(Currency $currency): int
            {
                // Defaulting to 2 decimal places (cents) for standard currency testing
                return 2;
            }

            public function isSubunitOf(Currency $currency, Currency $subunit): bool
            {
                return false;
            }

            public function smallestAmountFor(Currency $currency): Money
            {
                return new Money(1, $currency);
            }

            public function currencies(): iterable
            {
                return [];
            }
        };

        $this->currency = new Currency('USD');
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_throws_exception_when_fallback_currency_is_null(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        $this->expectException(ParserException::class);
        $this->expectExceptionMessage('DecimalMoneyParser cannot parse currency symbols. Use fallbackCurrency argument');

        $parser->parse('10.00');
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_returns_zero_money_for_empty_string(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        $result = $parser->parse('', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(0, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_throws_exception_for_invalid_format(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        $this->expectException(ParserException::class);
        $this->expectExceptionMessage('Cannot parse "abc" to Money.');

        $parser->parse('abc', $this->currency);
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_throws_exception_for_string_with_only_dot(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        $this->expectException(ParserException::class);
        $this->expectExceptionMessage('Cannot parse "." to Money.');

        $parser->parse('.', $this->currency);
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_positive_integer_amount(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '10' -> 10 dollars -> 1000 cents
        $result = $parser->parse('10', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(1000, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_positive_decimal_amount(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '10.50' -> 10 dollars and 50 cents -> 1050 cents
        $result = $parser->parse('10.50', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(1050, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_negative_integer_amount(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '-10' -> -10 dollars -> -1000 cents
        $result = $parser->parse('-10', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(-1000, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_negative_decimal_amount(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '-10.50' -> -10 dollars and 50 cents -> -1050 cents
        $result = $parser->parse('-10.50', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(-1050, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_fractional_digits_less_than_subunit(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '10.5' -> 10 dollars and 5 tenths of a cent? No, 5 in fraction position.
        // Logic: digits='10', fraction='5'. subunit=2.
        // decimal becomes '10' . '5' = '105'.
        // fractionDigits=1, subunit=2.
        // Pad with zeros: '105' . '' . '0' = '1050'.
        // Result: 1050 cents ($10.50).
        $result = $parser->parse('10.5', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(1050, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_fractional_digits_more_than_subunit(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '10.555' -> digits='10', fraction='555'. subunit=2.
        // decimal becomes '10' . '555' = '10555'.
        // fractionDigits=3, subunit=2.
        // Round logic in Number::roundMoneyValue needs to be traced or assumed standard rounding.
        // However, looking at the code:
        // $decimal = Number::roundMoneyValue($decimal, $subunit, $fractionDigits);
        // If fractionDigits > subunit, it truncates/pads?
        // Actually, let's look at the specific branch:
        // if ($fractionDigits > $subunit) { $decimal = substr($decimal, 0, $subunit - $fractionDigits); }
        // Wait, $subunit - $fractionDigits would be negative (2-3 = -1). substr(..., -1) takes last char.
        // This looks like a potential bug in the source or my understanding.
        // Let's re-read carefully:
        // $decimal .= $matches['fraction']; // '10555'
        // $decimal = Number::roundMoneyValue($decimal, $subunit, $fractionDigits);
        // If roundMoneyValue handles the precision, the subsequent substr might be redundant or defensive.
        // But wait, if roundMoneyValue returns an integer string, say '1056' (rounded), then:
        // fractionDigits (3) > subunit (2).
        // substr('1056', 0, 2-3) -> substr('1056', 0, -1) -> '105'.
        // This seems destructive. Let's assume standard behavior where extra precision is truncated/rounded.
        // Let's test a simpler case: '10.999' with subunit 2.
        // '10' . '999' = '10999'.
        // If roundMoneyValue rounds to nearest based on fractionDigits vs subunit...
        // Usually, parsers truncate or round. Let's assume the provided code works as intended for valid inputs.
        // A safer bet for "more than subunit" is often truncation in simple parsers unless specified.
        // Let's try '10.009' -> '10009'. Substr(0, -1) -> '100'. Amount 100 ($1.00).
        
        // Let's verify the substring logic again.
        // $subunit = 2. $fractionDigits = 3.
        // $subunit - $fractionDigits = -1.
        // substr('10009', 0, -1) is '1000'.
        // So '10.009' becomes 1000 cents ($10.00).
        
        $result = $parser->parse('10.009', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(1000, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_leading_zeros_in_digits(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '0010.50' -> digits='0010', fraction='50'.
        // decimal = '0010' . '50' = '001050'.
        // ltrim('001050', '0') = '1050'.
        $result = $parser->parse('0010.50', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(1050, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_leading_zeros_in_fraction(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '10.05' -> digits='10', fraction='05'.
        // decimal = '10' . '05' = '1005'.
        // fractionDigits=2, subunit=2. No padding/truncation.
        // ltrim('1005', '0') = '1005'.
        $result = $parser->parse('10.05', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(1005, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_small_amount_that_results_in_zero_after_truncation(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '0.001' -> digits='0', fraction='001'.
        // decimal = '0' . '001' = '0001'.
        // fractionDigits=3, subunit=2.
        // substr('0001', 0, -1) = '000'.
        // ltrim('000', '0') = ''.
        // If empty, set to '0'.
        $result = $parser->parse('0.001', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(0, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_negative_small_amount_that_results_in_zero_after_truncation(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '-0.001' -> digits='0', fraction='001', negative=true.
        // decimal = '-' . '0' = '-0'.
        // append fraction: '-0' . '001' = '-0001'.
        // fractionDigits=3, subunit=2.
        // substr('-0001', 0, -1) = '-000'.
        // Negative handling: '-' . ltrim(substr('-000', 1), '0') -> '-' . ltrim('000', '0') -> '-' . '' -> '-'.
        // If '-', set to '0'.
        $result = $parser->parse('-0.001', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(0, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_exact_subunit_digits(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '10.00' -> digits='10', fraction='00'.
        // decimal = '10' . '00' = '1000'.
        // fractionDigits=2, subunit=2. No change.
        // ltrim('1000', '0') = '1000'.
        $result = $parser->parse('10.00', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(1000, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_single_digit_integer_and_fraction(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '1.1' -> digits='1', fraction='1'.
        // decimal = '1' . '1' = '11'.
        // fractionDigits=1, subunit=2.
        // Pad: '11' . str_pad('', 1, '0') = '110'.
        // ltrim('110', '0') = '110'.
        $result = $parser->parse('1.1', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(110, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_just_fraction_part_as_zero_value(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '.5' -> matches digits=null? 
        // Pattern: /^(?P<sign>-)?(?P<digits>\d+)?\.?(?P<fraction>\d+)?$/
        // '.5' matches: sign='', digits=null, fraction='5'.
        // Code: if (! preg_match ... || ! isset($matches['digits'])) throw.
        // So '.5' throws exception because digits is not set.
        
        $this->expectException(ParserException::class);
        $this->expectExceptionMessage('Cannot parse ".5" to Money.');

        $parser->parse('.5', $this->currency);
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_whole_number_without_decimal_point(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '5' -> digits='5', fraction=null.
        // decimal = '5'.
        // No fraction branch.
        // decimal .= str_pad('', 2, '0') -> '500'.
        // ltrim('500', '0') = '500'.
        $result = $parser->parse('5', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(500, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_large_numbers(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '1000000.00'
        $result = $parser->parse('1000000.00', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(100000000, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_whitespace_padding(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // ' 10.50 '
        $result = $parser->parse(' 10.50 ', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(1050, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }

    #[Test]
    public function parse_handles_negative_zero_result(): void
    {
        $parser = new \Money\Parser\DecimalMoneyParser($this->currencies);

        // '-0.00'
        // digits='0', fraction='00', negative=true.
        // decimal = '-0' . '00' = '-000'.
        // fractionDigits=2, subunit=2. No pad/trunc.
        // Negative handling: '-' . ltrim(substr('-000', 1), '0') -> '-' . ltrim('00', '0') -> '-' . '' -> '-'.
        // Set to '0'.
        $result = $parser->parse('-0.00', $this->currency);

        self::assertSame(0, $result->getAmount());
        self::assertSame($this->currency, $result->getCurrency());
    }
}
```
